c-admin-recount.1.evidence: Set Help Desk member_count=999 and topic 176 reply_count=99 in the DB, then wp-admin Jetonomy Dashboard: button reads 'Recount totals' (#jetonomy-recount; the line says 'Recount counters'), click opens a confirm dialog 'Rebuild the topics, replies, members and vote counts from your content...' -> Confirm -> notice 'Counters rebuilt from your content.'; member_count back to 24 and reply_count 7 (true counts).

c-admin-recount.2.evidence: vote_score of topic 249 corrupted to 777; POST /admin/recount type=votes -> 200 {status:ok,updated:{post_vote_scores:1}}; score back to 0 = SUM(votes)

c-admin-recount.3.evidence: POST /admin/recount type=spaces -> 200 with updated space_post_counts / space_member_counts / category_space_counts; type=bogus -> 400 rest_invalid_param 'type is not one of all, posts, spaces, votes, and users'

c-admin-recount.4.evidence: Corrupted bob post_count=500; wp jetonomy recount --type=users printed 'user_post_counts: 2 rows / user_reply_counts: 0 rows / Success: Recount complete.'; profile count 14 = published topics 14

c-admin-recount.5.evidence: Set the home pulse transient to 999 members / 9,999 topics: a separate logged-out browser context showed '999 members 9,999 topics 77 this week'. After Recount totals -> Confirm, reloading the guest home reads '26 members 266 topics 54 this week' straight away (transient cleared by Cache::flush).

c-admin-recount.6.evidence: Dashboard 'Import Demo Data' (card on the Overview; confirm dialog) -> toast 'Demo data imported.'; a separate logged-out browser context read '5,010 members 1 topic' before and '5,029 members 210 topics' after a plain reload (no wait, no recount).

c-admin-recount.7.evidence: bbPress import of 2,000 topics (+750 replies) run to the end ('Import complete!'): a logged-out home immediately reads '5,027 members 4,404 topics' = published topics in public spaces (SQL 4,404) while the Overview reads '4,422 TOTAL TOPICS' (the 18 extra are topics in private/hidden spaces, which the guest total leaves out by design); no wait, the pulse transient is cleared by the import. The earlier 120-topic import also moved the guest home to '396 topics' at once.

c-admin-recount.8.evidence: Drifted counters (topic 176 reply_count 99, space 20 post_count 77, profile of bob post_count 55/reply_count 44, topic 338 reply_count 5), jetonomy_db_version set to 1.9.4.2, one /wp-admin/ request: version 2.0.7 and the queued recount backfill completed (jetonomy_recount_backfill done=true): reply_count 7 and 1, space 13, bob 25 posts / 81 replies - equal to COUNT(*) of the rows. The topic card reads '1 reply' (singular).

c-admin-recount.10.evidence: test_moderator POST /admin/recount -> 403 jetonomy_forbidden (button absence on Overview not viewed; his Overview URL loaded)

c-admin-recount.12.evidence: With 2,422 topics the Dashboard Recount totals -> Confirm completes (server ~0.3 s, no timeout) and Overview reads 2,422 TOTAL TOPICS; with the request delayed 2.5 s the button reads 'Recounting…' and is disabled while running, then returns to 'Recount totals' with the notice 'Counters rebuilt from your content.'; screenshot recount-running.png.

c-admin-recount.13.evidence: Double-click on the dialog's Confirm button sent exactly one POST /wp-json/jetonomy/v1/admin/recount; results stay correct (24 / 7).

c-admin-recount.14.evidence: Context offline, Recount totals -> Confirm: a dialog 'Unable to connect. Please check your Internet connection.' with OK appears, the button stays 'Recount totals' and enabled, counters unchanged; screenshot recount-offline.png.

c-admin-recount.15.evidence: bob's new topic (CLI create, no recount): the guest home pulse went 266 -> 267 topics (55 this week) and the admin Overview 283 -> 284 TOTAL TOPICS immediately - the write itself clears the pulse transient, so no recount is needed and the count is never stale by an hour.

c-admin-recount.17.evidence: wp jetonomy recount --type=users prints rows updated; wp jetonomy recount users -> 'Error: Too many positional arguments: users'

c-admin-recount.19.evidence: Offline recount failure shows 'Unable to connect. Please check your Internet connection.' (names the cause), not 'Could not get a valid response from the server.'.
